approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a population ranked by real accepted scores. It samples breeding parents across favored score quantiles, uses crossover and successive atom or bond mutations to fill a fresh pool, and checks molecular identity and novelty before admission. A Gaussian process fitted to all accepted task-local labels uses count fingerprints and correlated function draws to choose a unique evaluation batch. Real feedback updates the full training archive and greedily retained breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Each pool is currently discarded after its decision, including every valid molecule that was not selected.
approach.novelty: Give an unselected final molecule one more decision opportunity after real feedback, while generating the entire usual fresh pool first. Append eligible unselected molecules from only the preceding fresh pool in their original order, and let the existing selector decide over the union. Fresh occurrences win duplicate joins; older deferred molecules cannot be carried again. This tests proposal lifetime. The earlier prefix-harvesting sibling instead added intermediate products inside a fixed pool and reduced independent generation attempts; selector-removal, frozen-training and incumbent-targeting siblings changed different consumers. No unselected molecule becomes a label or a breeding parent.

observed_bottleneck: In n-62daf219c70a, Evolution.suggest constructs a local fresh pool, selects its evaluation batch, and retains only emitted records in pending/previous_emission; unselected valid finals have no later decision opportunity. Complete Parent summaries and run logs are available for every issued replica, with mean endpoint 0.5956696497334577 and population deviation 0.02659287062806747. Its published pool audit reports 435 full fresh pools and 69600 pooled records, of which 4350 are selected. This establishes the disposal behavior, not that disposal loses good molecules. n-7de8feaf821f keeps generated accepted labels out of later GP fits and loses 0.15185627363148665; its second batches change despite initially identical pools, supporting retention of real online predictive updates. n-01b48dd09404 removes predictive allocation while preserving full generation/model effort and loses 0.12438789088524467. Direct counterexamples constrain the hypothesis: n-79bc7a1dd0dc exposes 461 evaluated prefixes but reduces independent attempts from 75961 to 67373 and loses 0.040929502794467686; n-8a62df15e51f raises modeled incumbent-improvement utility but loses 0.05627557001043134, and fourteen of its modeled-zero choices nevertheless beat their real incumbent. None of these sources labels the Parent's unselected final proposals. The limiting behavior being tested is their one-decision lifetime, whose endpoint cost remains unestablished.
hypothesis: Extend each valid unselected fresh final proposal to exactly one later suggestion by appending the immediately preceding fresh pool's surviving unselected records after a fully generated current fresh pool, then apply the unchanged current accepted-only correlated posterior selector to that ordered union.

finding_summary.headline: One-round reconsideration produced local gains and descendants but lowered all three seed averages
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out missing exposure, failed revaluation and curtailed fresh output as explanations for the failed endpoint prediction. Useful delayed molecules and extensive descendant ancestry were insufficient to improve the full objective: most delayed evaluations still lost to their original best parent, and one task/seed had no delayed incumbent gain. The matched contrast rejects this fixed one-round lifetime rule under the tested composition; it does not isolate the cost of deferred competition from wider joint draws and the later adaptive trajectories. The passive fresh-only choices have no separately observed outcomes. The chemistry assessment likewise found more distinct core graphs without consistently better leading families: aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines remained prominent, and the strongest Parent arrangements were not reproduced in the tasks with the largest losses. Reactive local bonds, difficult ring geometry and undefined stereochemistry persist alongside more conventional high-scoring examples. Graph diversity and ancestor reachability therefore cannot stand in for reliable endpoint progress or plausible independent chemistry.
finding_summary.results: The lifetime mechanism ran with full fresh generation intact: all 435 decisions first produced 160 fresh proposals. Of 62,105 admitted deferred occurrences, every prediction changed after ten new real labels and 1,315 were evaluated. They produced 46 incumbent improvements; 593 later became breeders, and 2,797 accepted molecules had a delayed ancestor. Yet the complete mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.548956, a paired change of -0.046714 against the required +0.002 gain. All three seed averages were lower; nine of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell and six improved. The largest task-mean losses were sitagliptin_mpo (-0.147107) and deco_hop (-0.080214), while median_2 improved by 0.005534. Seed dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012479, around a lower mean. All formal evaluations completed within the unchanged budget and limits.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines span many ring graphs, but reactive bonds, difficult topology and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child and published Parent trajectories were read: each of the five objectives has 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer records across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2. No task or supplied trajectory path is missing. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true against n-62daf219c70a, with the same Search Seeds and no profile-mismatched seeds. This supports a complete descriptive chemistry comparison under the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task; it does not establish a component contribution or mechanism activation. The authoritative Parent artifacts are the published runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-62daf219c70a/seed-*/trajectories files, reached through the supplied artifact list and evidence index. The trusted citation list contains Child trajectories only, so cited_smiles below quote Child records; Parent examples are described with their published seed/evaluation references. The digest final_molecules excerpt is late seed-2 output, not every seed endpoint or every retained incumbent. Full trajectories supply the other seeds. The Child makes indole/pyridine ketones and thioamides, partially saturated aryl amides, linked nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycles, fluorinated amino-enones, cyclic and bridged aryl amines, and fluorinated imino/dione rings. The digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9598, 0.9701, 0.9724, 0.9828 and 0.9448 in the fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9552, 0.9701, 0.9644, 0.9736 and 0.9356. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts, aromatic-atom fractions or synthetic-feasibility measures. All charged-string and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0, despite visible protonatable amines and potential stereogenic centres. Bounded CPU RDKit inspection of the supplied graphs confirms substantial ring/topology variation: nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts in fixed task order are Child 300/146, 470/339, 431/293, 602/421 and 252/114; Parent counts are 294/123, 403/276, 390/258, 583/405 and 207/92. These graph descriptors count changed atom identities and ring connections, including questionable structures; they do not establish independent plausible chemical families. Per-seed high-score neighborhoods remain much narrower than the entire proposal set, while different seed families prevent a claim of global scaffold collapse. Accepted-parent reachability was separately traced in the supplied Child and published Parent logs without missing joins: visibly different aryl-amine leaders in the Child all reach the initial sulfonylated aryl/amide founder, for example. Such genealogical reachability does not prove atom retention, conserved scaffold identity, founder contribution or independent rediscovery. The descriptor and reachability audits are under .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot0-molecular/. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxides, terminal imines, unusual sulfur bonding and complicated unsaturated/bridged rings. Overall plausibility is therefore questionable rather than uniformly implausible: high-scoring conventional amine-containing and liability-free local-bond counterexamples exist. Scores and graph validity do not establish synthesis, stability, conformation, protonation state or biological activity. Historical gaps below retain their source in n-c55c3d520a2c through the n-62daf219c70a baseline; historical profile boundaries are not treated as new matched-effect evidence.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader at evaluation 281 has 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings: a dimethoxy substituted indole-like core connects through a methylene/thioamide segment to pyridine, with both an N-F bond and an N-Br thioamide nitrogen. Seed 1 instead reaches a 24-heavy-atom partially saturated quinoline-like carboxamide with a fluoropyridyl amide, hydroxymethyl group and two aromatic rings at evaluation 293; its other favored family is a diaryl pyrazoline carbothioamide. Seed 2 favors a 23-heavy-atom indole-like/pyridyl ketone with three aromatic rings, an imine substituent and N-OH at evaluation 215. These are medium-sized, heavily decorated aromatic frameworks, with substantially different local chemistry between seeds. The digest mean SMILES length is 42.6 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8356; this does not mean every leader is halogenated. The Parent leaders are related N-halogenated indole/enamine, hydroxamic-amide and aryl-diketone families (published seed 0/evaluation 289, seed 1/evaluation 293 and seed 2/evaluation 294). The Child seed-1 amide and seed-2 ordinary indole N-H relative offer more conventional local bonds than the reactive seed-0 leader.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader has nitrogen-bound fluorine and bromine, not just ordinary aryl halogens; its thioamide chemistry requires a separate stability and synthesis assessment.

Seed-2 terminal imines and N-OH/N-S relatives leave tautomerism and local reactivity unresolved, while the seed-1 pyrazoline relatives include halogenated saturated centres. These liabilities are not shared by every higher-scoring molecule.
Late zero-score tiny fragments still occur; ring richness and predominantly medium molecular size do not prevent loss of useful molecular context.
missing_features: The record does not establish dependable coverage of stable, alternative aromatic/polar-linkage arrangements across seeds. The partially saturated amide and ordinary indole N-H examples show that such chemistry is possible, so this is not an inability to make conventional heterocycles or amides.
Potential stereogenic saturated centres in the seed-1 family and imine configurations are not specified. No exact absent objective pharmacophore can be inferred from the observed scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed leaders score 0.42749549733373915, 0.41048050866648705 and 0.46058514794325744, respectively; the published Parent counterparts score 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. These are different adaptive molecules, not isolated local interventions. Within Child seed 2, the pyridyl ketone at evaluation 215 scores 0.46058514794325744, versus 0.43259502753313733 for the otherwise corresponding phenyl ketone at evaluation 282. Moving the pyridyl nitrogen to another position at evaluation 297 ties the leading value. The conventional indole N-H/methoxy relative at evaluation 186 scores 0.4470018114651393, demonstrating that an N-O or N-halogen bond is not needed for a nearby high score, although more than one substituent differs. Tiny N-F and water proposals score 0.0. The visible association is a combined aromatic/heteroaryl and polar-linkage arrangement with position-sensitive substitutions, not halogen count alone. The seed-2 final proposal falls to 0.22008791276595066 despite retaining its aromatic framework.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 reaches a 36-heavy-atom assembly of nitrogen-rich fused dione rings, a pyrazole bearing an aldehyde and an aza-aromatic fused carbocycle, linked through N-N/C-N-rich functionality at evaluation 239. Seed 1 reaches a much larger 48-heavy-atom, five-aromatic-ring assembly of aza/oxygen carbonyl heterocycles with terminal ethynyl, methoxy, carbonate and fluorinated alkenyl substituents at evaluation 288. Seed 2 instead reaches a 31-heavy-atom structure with four RDKit-perceived rings, only two aromatic: a fluorinated aminopyridyl group connects to a fused enone/pyridine/thioether-ether ring system, with an O-O-N=C substituent at evaluation 285. All provide rich rings and carbonyl functionality, but their local liabilities and synthetic complexity differ. The digest mean SMILES length is 70.9 and maximum is 216; oversized elaboration is visible beside more compact examples. Parent seed 0 instead finds a more compact fused nitrogen/carbonyl-thione assembly with O-F and a halogenated ether (published evaluation 281); Parent seed 1 favors a linked aza/oxygen-carbonyl, nitrile/cyanate family (evaluation 296), and Parent seed 2 a peroxide-bearing aryl/heteroaryl family with a small unsaturated fused ring (evaluation 296).
liabilities: The seed-2 leader contains an actual peroxide linkage and a terminal imine-containing extension; these are not ordinary ether substitutions. Carbon-bound fluorines in the same molecule should not be conflated with heteroatom-halogen liabilities.

The seed-0 leader contains N-N-rich linkages and an aldehyde; seed-1 combines multiple linked carbonyl heterocycles with a carbonate/enol-derived appendage and substantial size. Neither graph validity nor aromaticity supplies a synthesis route.

Large linked relatives and unusual ring closures increase conformational and synthetic complexity, while tiny late proposals discard the ring and functional-group relationships associated with higher scores.
missing_features: The Child does not reproduce the compact Parent seed-0 nitrogen/carbonyl-thione organization at a comparable observed score. That Parent structure itself has reactive attachments, so reproducing it verbatim would not establish good chemistry.

Stable peripheral alternatives and simpler connectivities that preserve favorable combined heterocyclic organization are not established across the leading families. The peroxide-free seed-2 example and tied seed-0 peripheral changes are useful counterexamples to a unique reactive-group requirement.
Stereochemical and conformational definition of the substituted saturated and fused-ring regions remains absent; the available scores do not identify a single required missing target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione/aryl molecule scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed leaders score 0.6045751633986929, 0.620561738208797 and 0.632992327365729; published Parent seed leaders score 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. In the Child seed-2 family, evaluation 232 lacks the peroxide appendage and scores 0.6217775245691497, while the O-O-N=C leader scores 0.632992327365729. Other substitutions also differ, so this is not a peroxide-effect estimate. The close O-O-vinyl relative at evaluation 277 scores 0.6223726900832276. A much larger joined relative at evaluation 298 scores 0.606537971225642; more molecular material does not guarantee a higher value. Seed-0 methyl-to-bromomethyl and N-ethyl-to-N-propyl variants tie its leader at 0.6045751633986929. Small fluoroacetaldehyde and ethene proposals sit at 0.5, showing that this observed floor is not evidence of useful chemistry. These associations favor a particular combined heterocyclic organization and tolerate some peripheral substitutions. The larger Child seed-0 assembly does not reproduce the higher-scoring compact Parent organization.

per_task.generated_character: Accessible aliphatic amines are already abundant in the better molecules. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 294 has 25 heavy atoms, two aromatic regions, phenol, aryl chloride and propyl substituents, and a densely connected cyclic amine region; a less cross-linked relative at evaluation 246 contains an available secondary methylamine and a tetrahydroisoquinoline-like ring. Seed 1 favors a 26-heavy-atom fluorophenol/benzyl framework with a bridged cyclic ether and pyrrolidine-containing amine at evaluation 222. Seed 2 favors a 29-heavy-atom aminoaryl ether, an aliphatic amine and N-aryl azetidine, with several carbon-bound halogens and a chemically unusual C#S-C terminus at evaluation 285. The digest halogen-string incidence is 0.9828 and mean SMILES length is 51.9. Published Parent leaders instead include a flexible tertiary bis-aryl amine (seed 0/evaluation 284), an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine/cyclic aryl ether (seed 1/evaluation 261), and a biaryl fused thioether with pyrrolidine (seed 2/evaluation 241). Thus useful amines and several scaffold organizations are represented on both sides. Accepted-parent ancestry of the visibly different Child leaders returns to the same initial sulfonylated aryl/amide molecule; this does not mean its whole scaffold remains intact.
liabilities: Complicated bridges and small fused nitrogen rings appear beside more conventional amines. Ring perception cannot establish accessible geometry or a selective synthesis.
The seed-2 terminal carbon-sulfur triple bond with further sulfur substitution is distinct from a normal thioether or thiocarbonyl and warrants a specific valence/reactivity assessment.

Potential stereogenic centres are unassigned. Some late relatives introduce N-Br or S-Br bonds, benzylic bromide, and heavy carbon-bound halogen substitution; these are local liabilities, not properties of every high-scoring aryl amine.
missing_features: The missing capability is stereochemically and geometrically defined versions of successful saturated/bridged aryl-amine arrangements, not the ability to produce basic amines or nitrogen rings.

The seed-2 trajectory lacks a demonstrated equally scoring conventional local replacement for its unusual C#S-C terminus; the nearby high-scoring aminomethyl cyclic example shows that the broader amine/aromatic organization can survive without it.

Protonation-state identity is unresolved in the neutral strings. Zero formal-charge incidence does not imply absence of protonatable nitrogen, and the scores do not reveal an exact additional required pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine fragment at Child seed 0/evaluation 16 scores 0.00021169315013374197, despite possessing a nitrogen ring, aromatic ring and chlorines. Child seed leaders score 0.9999902752652226, 0.995264102605631 and 0.9749506155555931; the published Parent leaders score 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012. The Child seed-0 less cross-linked amine at evaluation 246 already scores 0.9953251127190992, and the seed-1 bridged ether/pyrrolidine leader lacks N-halogen and O-halogen bonds. Available aliphatic amines arranged with aromatic surfaces are associated with the high end of this sample; nitrogen count or halogenation alone is insufficient. The seed-2 C#S-C-bearing azetidine relatives at evaluations 285 and 292 tie despite exchanging one aryl chlorine for fluorine, and a different aminomethyl cyclic analogue at evaluation 297 scores 0.9710229447939221 without the C#S-C terminus. Therefore unusual sulfur bonding is not shown to be necessary. These near-ceiling supplied scores do not certify affinity, selectivity or geometric feasibility.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 reaches a 30-heavy-atom quinoline/pyrrole assembly attached to a bridged dicarbonyl amine/lactam region at evaluation 293. Seed 1 reaches a 34-heavy-atom propyl/ethoxy substituted polyaromatic nitrogen framework tethered to a dicarbonyl amine/lactam segment at evaluation 295. Seed 2 instead links propylquinoline to ethoxy-substituted nitrogen/carbonyl rings and an unsaturated small fused ring at evaluation 283, also with 34 heavy atoms. The digest mean SMILES length is 55.7 and halogen-string incidence is only 0.1644. Carbonyls, nitrogen atoms and aromatic regions are well represented; the unusual ring connections are the principal plausibility question. The published Parent seed-0 leader uses a bridged diaryl lactam with N-O connectivity (evaluation 293), while seed-1 and seed-2 leaders use quinoline-linked amino/ether and dicarbonyl rings (evaluations 278 and 261). These are related chemical neighborhoods with substantial ring rewiring, rather than an absence of ring generation.
liabilities: Dense bridges, unsaturated small rings and medium/large ring closures pose geometry and synthesis questions, even when heavy-atom count remains moderate.

Near-leading relatives introduce N-F and sulfur-containing N-S/ring segments; the leading molecule itself lacks an N-halogen bond, so reactive bonds should not be treated as necessary for the observed score.
Potential stereocentres are unspecified and extensive ring rewiring changes conformational freedom in ways that an aromatic-string counter cannot describe.
missing_features: The leading graphs lack demonstrated geometrically credible and synthetically accessible alternatives that preserve the observed aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization. The record does not justify simply adding further rings or heteroatoms.

Stereochemical definition of saturated bridges and conformational definition of medium or large ring closures are absent. The unusual aromatic-labelled medium ring especially needs evidence beyond SMILES perception.

Independent plausible alternatives within each seed high-score neighborhood remain unestablished. Numerous changed Murcko graphs and mixed founder reachability are not interchangeable with useful scaffold independence.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 reaches a 29-heavy-atom ester-substituted aryl/nitrogen-carbonyl assembly bearing N-F and C=N-O-F functionality, with a cyclopropene-containing bridge and medium-ring connectivity at evaluation 223. Seed 1 favors a 28-heavy-atom aryl phenol attached to a fused dione/N-fluoro heterocycle and fluorinated dihydrofuran substituent at evaluation 271. Seed 2 favors a 26-heavy-atom fused/bridged imino-carbonyl nitrogen system attached to phenol, bearing N-F and carbon-bound fluoromethyl groups at evaluation 241. The seed-2 family also produces a less bridged three-aromatic-ring relative at evaluation 272. These are compact, nitrogen-rich and strongly fluorinated graphs; the digest mean SMILES length is 47.2 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8966. Published Parent seed-0 and seed-1 leaders are related aryl imino/dione heterocycles with fluorinated substituents (evaluations 276 and 290), while Parent seed 2 reaches a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring attached to a small cyclic cumulene (evaluation 273). liabilities: Nitrogen-bound fluorine and the seed-0 N-O-F sequence raise specific reactivity concerns that ordinary C-F bonds do not share.

The cyclopropene-containing bridged graph and densely fused/bridged nitrogen rings need geometric and synthetic validation; removal of the Parent small cyclic cumulene does not make all Child ring topologies credible.

Potential stereogenic centres and imine configuration are unspecified. Tiny late fluorine, halogen and sulfur-containing fragments provide extremely small scores despite abundant halogen-string incidence overall.
missing_features: Geometrically credible, stable alternatives that retain the favorable compact polar/aryl arrangement are not consistently demonstrated. The Child lacks the Parent seed-2 leading organization, but that Parent cyclic-cumulene graph is itself a chemical liability rather than a design prescription.

The best examples do not establish control of local substitution while maintaining conventional bond environments: N-F and O-F recur, although a high-scoring N-fluoroalkyl counterexample demonstrates that N-halogen bonding is not universal.

Tautomeric, stereochemical and conformational identities of imino/carbonyl heterocycles and bridged substituted rings remain unresolved. No exact hidden-objective pharmacophore can be inferred from these records.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The qualitative gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and retained through its n-62daf219c70a baseline; the present observation is n-7652d7030abe against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the frozen epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per independent objective. This preserves the source and profile boundary rather than claiming a historical matched component effect. Current higher-scoring families include N-F/N-Br bonds, N-O-F, peroxides, terminal imines and an unusual C#S-C segment. Counterexamples are material: an ordinary indole N-H ketone, a partly saturated aryl carboxamide, conventional cyclic aryl amines, a peroxide-free amino-enone and an N-fluoroalkyl imino-carbonyl relative also carry useful observed scores. Ordinary carbon-bound halogens and available amines are already generated. The concern is environment-specific reliability, not a universal missing functional group or a rule that every heteroatom bond is undesirable.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while exploring otherwise useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need environment-aware local transformations and conventional bonding alternatives that preserve favorable structural relationships learned from its own accepted feedback. Evaluate such alternatives rather than prescribing a target motif or assuming a blanket functional-group filter improves scores. These output associations do not identify which retained component caused the liabilities or whether proposal lifetime changes their frequency causally.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The qualitative gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and retained through its n-62daf219c70a baseline; the present observation is n-7652d7030abe against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the frozen epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per independent objective. This preserves the source and profile boundary rather than claiming a historical matched component effect. The Child retains dense bridges, unsaturated small rings, medium-ring closures and a large aromatic-labelled ring in its leading structures; a cyclopropene-containing bridge is another visible example. The Parent small cyclic-cumulene leader is not reproduced by the corresponding Child leader, so that exact liability must not be transferred as if it persisted unchanged. Conventional saturated cyclic amines and less cross-linked high-scoring relatives are counterexamples to any claim that difficult geometry is required. Rich ring-string incidence and numerous typed or generic scaffold graphs do not provide conformational feasibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish a valid ring graph from a geometrically and synthetically credible ring arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need a way to preserve useful relationships while accounting for ring size, unsaturation, bridge connectivity and accessible conformation. Plausible alternative connectivities would test this gap without a blanket prohibition on small rings, fusion or ring formation. A chemical feasibility concern is not an observed score penalty and cannot be attributed to a particular mechanism from these trajectories alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The qualitative gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and retained through its n-62daf219c70a baseline; the present observation is n-7652d7030abe against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the frozen epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per independent objective. This preserves the source and profile boundary rather than claiming a historical matched component effect. Every supplied task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, while the evaluated cyclic amines, fluorinated saturated centres and bridged frameworks contain potential stereogenic environments. Imines and unsaturated linkers also lack explicit configurational definition. Some aromatic or otherwise achiral examples do not need such assignments; zero formal-charge-string incidence is a separate observation and does not negate visibly protonatable aliphatic amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not resolve stereochemical identity when proposing potentially stereogenic saturated, bridged or imine-containing structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations would need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemical possibilities when a generated structure requires them, while handling achiral and configurationally labile cases appropriately. Protonation and tautomer identity should be assessed separately. The records show unresolved chemical identity, not a measured stereochemical score advantage or evidence that one search component caused the omission.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The qualitative gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and retained through its n-62daf219c70a baseline; the present observation is n-7652d7030abe against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the frozen epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per independent objective. This preserves the source and profile boundary rather than claiming a historical matched component effect. Tiny late fragments remain in the evaluated trajectories while higher scores occur for combined aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl arrangements. Large linked or more cross-linked relatives can score below more compact members of the same neighborhood. Conversely, compact ordinary amines, a peroxide-free amino-enone and shorter ring relatives retain useful scores, so useful simplification is already possible. Many distinct Murcko graphs coexist with related leading chemical families; accepted-parent reachability and changed SMILES do not prove chemically independent alternatives or founder contribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control over loss of functional-group context and excessive elaboration of otherwise useful structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local accepted feedback could guide context-preserving replacement and simplification while allowing distinct plausible connectivities. The missing capability is consistent control of what is retained during size and topology changes, not an inability to generate small molecules or rings. Neither a fixed minimum size, automatic molecular growth, nor more distinct graph strings is supported as an objective-improving rule; any such change requires its own conditioned evidence.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
